column2: At the end of twenty-nine, "ga" would be (the measure); "gu" is a single long, by the count of syllables reversed from ten.
By the reversed placing of the Pathya, a Chapala, or the even sound; a Vipula with the seventh (foot) even — all of that same and of it;
or the Vipula in those two; the Chakra class is declared; there would be four feet and above, with increase by four in the feet;
ending with two longs, Apida; Pratyapida, Ganadika; by reversal of the first, Manjari, Lavani in order;
the one called Amritadhara; now Uddhata and the rest are told: on one side Samajasana would be, not "sau jo go", then "bha nau na jau";
no go, then "sa ja sa", "go ga" of the third foot; in Saurabha some "na bha ga"; Lalita "na ma jau sa";
Upasthita, Prachupita — the first and so on "sama jau sa"; "go ga" then "ma la ja", Roga; Sama "na ga ra ja yah" in the foot;
Vardhamana "ma lau sva na sau"; then Bhoja and the rest are told; I shall tell the pure Virad, called Arshabha, and the half-equal...
Drutavilambita would be "na bha bha ra" — then "na la" (formula listing). Shripuṭa "va su ve da" — jalogati, jala, "ja ma";
ja sa and "va sa ra va" and "tata nanamara" are remembered. Kusumavichitra "na yau, dyau nau nau rau" — Chalambika;
Bhujangaprayata with four "tha"; Sragvini born of the same; Pramitakshara "ga jau sau"; Kantotpida held "sa mau sama";
Vaishvadevi "ma ma ya ya" five-limbed; Navamalini "na jau bha yau" each foot, if Jagati too;
Praharshini "ma va ja va" — Gopati and the fire-directions; Ruchira "ja bha sa ja ga" cut by four (and) nine is remembered;
Mattamayura "ma ta ya sa ga", caesura at four and nine; Gauri "na la na sa ga"; Asambadha "na ta na ga";
go ga indriya navakau nanau vasanagah svarah; Aparajita "na na bha na na ga" — notes;
Prahara-nakalita twice; Vasantatilaka "na bha"; "ja gau" — Simhonnata, that is the sage's Uddharshini;
Chandravarta "na nau", Somavarta is remembered nine and sixth; Manigunanikara "sau"; Malini "nau mayau ya yah";
caesura eight, vowel; "bha vau na ta la mitra sagrahah"; Rishabhagajavilasita is to be known; Shikharini "ja gau";
rasa bhala bhrigu rudra; Prithvi "ja sa ja sa ja nau"; "go vasugraha vichchhinna" told by Pingala of old;
Vamshapatrapatita would be "bha na bha ga sa dik"; Harini "na sa ma ra sa na ga" — six, four, vowels;
Mandakranta "na bha na ta ta ga gah" ten, six, seven; Kusumitalata, Vellita "ya ya yah"; arrows (five);
chariots (six), vowels; Pratirathasa-sajasah; Shardulavikridita — caesura twelve and seven;
Kriti, Suvadana, "mo ra bha na ya bha na ga" — gods; caesura — thus the metres are remembered in order;
Sragdhara "ma ra bha na ya ya ya" with caesura three times seven; Samudraka "bha ra ja na vo na ga" — ten, twelve;
Ashvalalita "na ja bha ja bha ja"; "bha na ma ishatah"; Mattakrida "ma ma na na na na ga"; Atithi...
Tanvi "bha na ta sa bho bho la"; arrows, suras, suns; Krauñchapada "bha ma ta ta nau nau" — five, arrows, eight;
Bhujangavijrimbhita "ma ma ta na na va sa nau"; the cut with ... — the Upahara is thus;
ma na na na ta na sa ga gau — nine, six; "nau sapta ro" — Dandada, Chandavrishti-praghataka;
by increase of "ra" the Vyala, Jimuta and the rest; in the rest they are to be known as Prachita; the Gatha-prastara is declared.
It produces the letters; their division is remembered as fivefold: by vowel, by time, by place, by effort, by meaning-giving;
eight are the places of letters: chest, throat, head, root of tongue, teeth, nose, lips and palate.
Natural state and openness: sha, sha, sa and ra; the tongue-root and upadhmaniya — eightfold is the movement of the sibilant;
the verse, the joining of feeling, beginning with "u" the supreme state; ending with a vowel such as that one should know; whatever else is manifest of the sibilant.
What comes from a wrong place is burned and mispronounced and eaten (swallowed); thus pronunciation is sin; thus pronunciation is auspicious —
what comes from the right place is well arranged with the Veda tradition, used with a good voice and good mouth, to the Brahmin-king.
One who is dreadful, long-lipped, unclear, nasal, stammering or many-tongued is not fit to speak the letters.
Thus letters should be used, neither unclear nor pressed; by right use of letters one is honored in Brahma's world.
Udatta, anudatta and svarita are the three accents; short, long and prolonged by time up to the limit of rule.
Guttural are a, ha, visarga, ka-series; palatal e, i, cha-series, ya, sha; labial u, pa-series, va; cerebral ri, ra, sha; dental lri, la, sa are remembered;
at the root of the tongue "h" is told; the dental-labial is "v" by the wise; e and ai guttural-palatal; o and au guttural-labial are remembered;
half a mora of the guttural belongs to e and ai; the ayogavaha are to be known as sharing the place of support.
Vowels are untouched; semivowels slightly; stops are the touched consonants; the rest are said to be touched consonants — know this chiefly.
The nasals and "m"; the first of the voiced and ha, sha, sa; slightly voiced the semivowels; the thakara and the rest unvoiced; know slightly breathy vowel — they call it long.
Where there is praise of the doer's lineage in prose at length, and abduction of a maiden, battle, separation and calamities,
where brilliant styles, modes and activities are, and where the division is by chapters (uchchhvasa), and what is Churnaka-uttara,
either front or other opening — that is remembered as an Akhyayika; where the poet briefly praises his own line in verses,
where there is another tale for the descent of the main matter, where there is no chapter-division, sometimes by Alambhakas —
that is called Katha; in its womb one should bind a four-line verse. A partial tale is Khandakatha; Parikatha is the other of the two;
the minister, or a trader, or a Brahmin they know as hero; of them know pathos, and separation fourfold;
the first of them is not completed, it runs after the Katha; by mixture of Katha and Akhyayika it is remembered as Parikatha.
The terrible, the happy, and the pathetic sentiment in the womb; the marvelous at the end, well-arranged in meaning, not exalted — that is Kathanika.
Verse is four-footed, and that is threefold: Vritta, Jati; Vritta is counted by syllable number, that is Uktha, arisen from Kriti and remainder;
by moras counting is Jati, says Kashyapa. Equal, half-equal, unequal — Vritta is threefold by Pingala.
That knowledge is a boat for those wishing to cross the deep ocean of poetry. Mahakavya, Kalapa, Paryabandha, Vishesaka,
Kulaka, Muktaka, Kosha — these are the family of verse. A Mahakavya is a work in cantos begun in Sanskrit;
not abandoning identity there, what equals it is not much faulted; arisen from history or tale, or otherwise good in its refuge;
fixed on counsel, envoy, march and battle, not too long. With Shakvari, Atijagati, Atishakvari and Trishtubh,
with Pushpitagra and the rest, with Vakra and Abhijana, charming and equal; free, ending in another meter, cantos not too short;
another canto with Atisharvarika and Ashti, singly mixed; by mora too another; and the last among the most excellent;
a doubtless kalpa is greatly blamed in it; special disregard by the good. With city, ocean, mountain, season, moon, sun, hermitage and tree,
garden, water-sport, honey-drinking and love-festivals, with arrangement of the messenger's words, with marvels of the deeds of unchaste women,
with darkness, wind and other very full accessories; engaged in all modes, imbued with all feelings,
nourished with all styles and sentiments, adorned with nourished qualities — therefore it is a great poem, and its maker a great poet.
Even where skill in speech is primary, sentiment alone is the life here; produced by separate effort in the curve of speech, the body from sentiment;
the fruit of the four aims, described by the hero's name; Kaishiki style, tender, with equal conduct;
Kalapa here: absence; earlier the sentiment called love; with Vishesaka, attainment and the rest, by Sanskrit and by the eye;
Kulaka would be with many verses; those joined (Sandanitaka); Muktaka is a single verse, able to astonish the good;
joined with fine sayings of lion-poets and with beauties; Kosha, unlimited, Brahma, pleases the cultured.
Appearance, simile, power, and in the canto what is of different meter; mixed body is renowned; Prakirna is twofold: to be heard and to be acted; Prakirna with all utterances.
Salutation to gods and praise of teachers, and blessings of cows, Brahmins, kings and the like are sung;
at the end of the Nandi, the stage-manager (sutradhara) is bound in the plays. The order of teachers, praise of lineage, the poet's manhood,
and relation and meaning of the poem — he should declare these five. The actress, jester, or attendant
together with the stage-manager hold a conversation, with various speeches arising from their own business, mutually involving the matter in hand —
that is to be known by the wise as Amukha; it is also the prelude (prastavana). Pravrittaka, Kathodghata and Prayogatishaya;
Amukha has three kinds, arising in the seed-parts; relying on the time begun, the stage-manager would describe...
